Locking, concurrency, sleep and ownership rules for TEE, trace, socket and USB paths are not shown.

findings.text: TEE parameter attribute encoding reserves a meta flag at hex 100. The attribute mask combines the type mask with that meta flag, so one test isolates kind plus meta.

TEE client login identifies authentication context. Public is zero, user one, group two, application four, user-application five, group-application six. Rich-OS kernel login occupies a high range from 80000000 hex to BFFFFFFF hex, with the base kernel login equal to the range minimum.
TEE generic parameter holds four 64-bit slots: an attribute word plus three value slots a, b and c. UUIDs used with TEE ioctls are sixteen bytes long.

Open-session argument carries trusted-application UUID and client UUID of sixteen bytes each, plus client login, cancel identifier, session handle output, return code and origin, a parameter count, and a trailing variable parameter array whose length equals that count.
Invoke argument identifies target function and session, carries cancel identifier, return code and origin, parameter count, and a trailing variable parameter array sized by that count.
Cancel argument pairs a cancel identifier with a session handle. Close-session argument carries only the session handle.
Supplicant receive argument carries function identifier, parameter count and trailing parameter array. Supplicant send argument carries return value, parameter count and trailing parameter array.

Shared-memory registration by address carries 64-bit address and length, 32-bit flags and signed 32-bit identifier. Registration by file descriptor carries signed 64-bit descriptor, 64-bit size, flags and identifier.
Object invoke argument carries 64-bit object identifier, 32-bit operation, 32-bit return, 32-bit parameter count, 32-bit padding, and a trailing variable parameter array sized by the count.

TEE user interface exposes ioctls for opening a session, invoking a command, cancelling, closing a session, supplicant receive and send, shared-memory registration by address and by descriptor, and object invocation. Session, invoke, cancel, supplicant and object operations use read-direction ioctls; shared-memory registrations use read-write ioctls; each binds a specific argument structure.

TEE session lifecycle starts with open, which outputs a session handle and return status, continues through repeated invoke or object operations on that handle with optional cancel by cancel identifier, and ends with close consuming the handle. Supplicant interaction is a paired receive then send exchange carrying function, parameters and return status.

Trace mapped-meta header records meta page size and header length, sub-buffer size and count, a nested reader record with lost events, identifier and read position, flags, entry and overrun and read counters, and pages lost and touched counters.
Trace mapping interface provides a get-reader ioctl built from group R and code hex 20 to obtain reader state.

Kernel UAPI integer limits define signed int maximum from an all-ones unsigned shift and minimum as negative maximum minus one. Signed and unsigned 128-bit integers are 16-byte aligned. Bitwise annotation marks endian and checksum types: little and big endian 16, 32 and 64-bit plus 16-bit sum and 32-bit wide sum. Aligned 64-bit helpers force 8-byte alignment for signed, unsigned and endian variants; poll type is an unsigned bitwise type.
UDP header holds four 16-bit network-order fields: source port, destination port, length and checksum.

UDP socket options include cork at one to avoid partial segments, encapsulation mode at 100, no-checksum transmit and receive for v6 at 101 and 102, segment size at 103 and GRO reception at 104. Encapsulation payload types span one through eight covering non-IKE ESP, ESP in UDP, L2TP, GTP zero and GTP-U, RXRPC, ESP in TCP, and OpenVPN in UDP.

Vector I/O element pairs a user pointer base with a kernel size length. Device-memory fragment message records fragment offset, size, token, buffer identifier and flags. Token range records start and count.
Fast inline vector count is eight; maximum vector count is 1024.
Unix domain socket address holds an address family plus a byte pathname whose capacity is 108. A private protocol ioctl opens a socket file with path-only semantics.

USB control direction uses zero for host-to-device and hex 80 for device-to-host. Request type occupies two bits shifted by five with standard, class, vendor and reserved encodings and a mask. Recipient uses low five bits with device, interface, endpoint, other, port and R-pipe values plus mask.

Standard USB requests include status, feature, address, descriptor, configuration and interface operations, sync frame, SEL and isoch delay, plus wireless, security, handshake, connection, data, loopback, interface DS and authentication operations. Power-delivery extensions add partner PDO, battery status, PDO setting and vendor message get and send with decimal codes twenty through twenty-four.

USB device feature selectors cover self power, remote wakeup, test mode and battery sharing, HNP enable and support variants, wireless device, alternate HNP, debug mode and bulk max-packet update. Test modes J, K, SE0-NAK, packet and force-enable use one through five. Status type distinguishes standard zero from PTM one. Link selectors enable U1, U2 and LTM with matching status bits. Function suspend uses selector zero with low-power and remote-wakeup option bits and capability and state bits; endpoint halt is zero. Battery and power-delivery selectors span wake mask, PD awareness, policy, role swap, goto-min, return power, accept and reject, resets, change and charging policy.

USB control request is eight bytes: type, request, value, index and length with little-endian words and packed layout. Generic header is length plus type. Device descriptor carries version, class triple, max packet, vendor, product and device versions, string indices and configuration count with total size eighteen. Configuration descriptor carries total length, interface count, value, string index, attributes and power with size nine. Interface descriptor carries number, alternate, endpoint count, class triple and string index with size nine. Endpoint descriptor carries address, attributes, max packet, interval and audio-only refresh and sync address with sizes seven and nine for audio. String descriptor is length plus type plus a union of legacy padding or flexible UTF-16LE data.

USB descriptor type codes assign device through endpoint, qualifier, other-speed, power, OTG, debug, association, security, key, encryption, BOS, capability, wireless companion, embedded isochron companion, wire adapter and DFU sharing hex 21, R-pipe, radio control, pipe usage, superspeed companion and superspeed-plus isochron companion. Class-specific device, configuration, string, interface and endpoint types combine class bits with the base type.

USB class codes span per-interface zero, audio, comm, HID, physical, still image, printer, mass storage, hub, CDC data, smart card, content security, video, wireless controller, healthcare, audio-video, billboard, type-C bridge, MCTP, misc, application-specific and vendor-specific with DFU and vendor subclasses. Configuration attributes require bit seven set and define self-power, wakeup and battery bits. Maximum string length is 126. Endpoint masks isolate number, direction and transfer type with control, isochronous, bulk and interrupt encodings, adjustable-max flag, max-packet mask and multiplier shift, mask and extractor.

TEE variable parameter arrays are governed by accompanying counts; consumers treat the count as element count, not byte size. USB descriptors are packed with explicit length and size constants; audio endpoints use audio size in length rather than native structure size; configuration attribute bit seven is always set. Unix pathname never exceeds its bound; vector count never exceeds maximum; trace meta fields describe shared sub-buffer geometry.

Unbounded count and length fields risk overrun if trusted without validation: TEE parameter counts sizing flexible arrays, shared-memory address and length or descriptor size, trace reader and overrun counters in shared memory, Unix pathname without guaranteed termination, vector lengths and dmabuf offsets, and USB length and packet fields from devices.
UAPI headers use include guards to ensure single inclusion for termios, trace mapping, type limits, base types, UDP, vector I/O, Unix sockets, unistd and USB chapter nine definitions.
